title: Specialist lender provides £1.9m bridging loan for Watford barn
summary:
Specialist lender Glenhawk has provided a £1.9 million regulated bridging loan secured against a converted barn in Watford, allowing the borrower additional time to market the property. The facility was arranged at 66% loan-to-value and refinanced both a first and second charge on the residential property.

title: Bridging loan releases equity for shopping centre purchase
summary:
StreamBank has provided a £1.5 million bridging loan to fund an experienced property investor's acquisition of a £3 million shopping centre in Peterlee, County Durham. The 12-month facility was secured against a residential property in Ashbourne, Derbyshire, enabling the borrower to bridge a funding gap after commercial finance covered the majority of the purchase.

title: Developer secures £822,000 exit finance in Sydenham
summary:
A specialist lender has provided £822,000 in developer exit finance for a residential scheme in Sydenham, South East London. The 12-month loan at 70% LTV is secured against two unsold flats in an eight-unit development.

title: Tenant referencing gains prominence as CCJs rise 11.6%
summary:
Landlords across England and Wales are placing greater emphasis on tenant referencing procedures following restrictions on advance rent payments and a significant rise in County Court Judgements. Data shows nearly 1.02 million new consumer CCJs were registered in 2025, an 11.6% annual increase.

title: Property software firm highlights due diligence risks
summary:
Estate agency software provider Veco has highlighted the importance of robust systems and processes for agencies considering growth or eventual sale, pointing to compliance records and operational dependencies as key areas of buyer scrutiny during due diligence.

title: Burnham announces housing reforms targeting landlords
summary:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has outlined housing policy measures at the Labour Party Conference, including reforms to first-time buyer schemes, leasehold legislation, and new powers for councils to address empty and substandard properties.

title: Government confirms regulation of leasehold managing agents
summary:
The UK government has confirmed plans to introduce mandatory regulation of leasehold managing agents, requiring them to obtain licences and meet professional standards. The measures will also cap fees charged by freeholders for granting permissions and administrative services.

title: UK mortgage approvals fall to 32-month low in August
summary:
Mortgage approvals for UK home purchases dropped to their lowest level in 32 months during August, as geopolitical tensions contributed to rising borrowing costs. Just 54,918 mortgages for new home purchases were approved, the lowest monthly total since December 2023.

title: Government confirms mandatory licensing for property agents
summary:
The government has confirmed plans to introduce independent regulation of property agents, requiring estate and letting agents to hold licences and appropriate qualifications to operate. Under the proposals, an independent regulator would have the power to withdraw licences from agents who fail to meet required standards.

title: Subsidence claim delays raise questions for homeowners
summary:
A London family has been waiting three years for LV= General Insurance to complete repairs following a subsidence claim. The case highlights growing challenges in property insurance as subsidence claims rise across the UK due to drought conditions.
